display.purpose: The page’s single largest statement. Hero only, one per page. Weight 400 with -0.04em tracking.

headline.purpose: Major section openers — What We Do, How It Works, Results, closing CTA.

body.purpose: All reading copy. Measure caps around 65–75ch.

label.purpose: The mono margin voice: counters, section markers, tags, metadata. Never a headline, never body, never an eyebrow above a title.

quote.purpose: HV Fitzgerald serif. The rarest thing in the system — elevated statements only.

shadows.name: none
shadows.purpose: The system ships zero elevation shadows. Shadow tokens were removed from the scale deliberately. Depth is canvas contrast plus a 1px hairline.

shadows.name: focus-ring
shadows.purpose: Form control focus. A ring, not elevation: no blur, no offset.

shadows.name: focus-ring-invalid
shadows.purpose: Focus ring on a control in the invalid state.

shadows.name: nav-glass
shadows.purpose: Not a shadow. The only spatial effect in the system: the floating nav shells read as glass, changing tint rather than altitude.

motion.name: dur-fast
motion.purpose: State changes: hover lift, color and border transitions.

motion.name: dur-base
motion.purpose: Canvas and tone transitions, including the nav tone flip and disclosure collapse.

motion.name: dur-reveal
motion.purpose: Scroll reveals, and the arrow flyby — slow on purpose so the travel actually reads.

motion.name: ease-standard
motion.purpose: Restrained ease-out. The default for state transitions.

motion.name: ease-inout
motion.purpose: Symmetric easing, used on disclosure collapse.

motion.name: ease-editorial
motion.purpose: Long, settled reveals. The house curve for anything that arrives rather than reacts.

components.name: Primary Button

narrative.overview:
Bianomics sells the layer underneath the visible result: everything people notice about you was decided somewhere they can't see. The Drafting Room is that somewhere, made into an interface. The page does not present conclusions the way a portfolio does; it shows the working surface where conclusions get made. Sections carry numbers. Labels sit out in the margin in monospace, annotating rather than announcing. Rules are single hairlines. The four practice colors behave like a legend on a technical drawing: a color appears because the thing it marks belongs to that practice, never because a card needed brightening.

The material is paper and ink, and it is never perfectly clean. A fine grain sits fixed over the entire viewport so the page reads as a printed surface rather than a rendered one; a blue haze occupies the right side of the light canvas; halftone dot screens fade in and out of section transitions like a press screen. Depth is entirely honest — there are no shadows anywhere in the system, and the shadow tokens were removed on purpose. What separates one plane from another is canvas contrast and a 1px hairline, nothing else.

Type carries the authority. Headings run at a single weight (400) across the whole site and get their hierarchy from size and negative tracking, which is why the display type reads as chiselled rather than shouted. Two weights ship in total: 400 for everything read, 600 for small UI that has to be picked out. Controls are quiet until touched — flat and still at rest, then answering precisely: a 2px lift, an arrow that flies out of its badge while its twin flies in, glass chrome that re-tints against whichever canvas has scrolled underneath it.
keyCharacteristics: Paper is home; near-black is punctuation that has to earn its place.
Zero shadows. Depth is canvas contrast plus one hairline.
One weight for every heading (400). Size and tracking carry the hierarchy.
Monospace is the margin voice, never the headline and never the body.
Four practice colors used as a legend, one CTA color site-wide.
Every surface is textured. A flat, clean plane is off-system.
Sharp content surfaces (4px), blocky controls (8px), pills reserved for tags.

rules.name: The Legend Rule
rules.body: The four practice colors are an index, not a palette. A color appears on an element because that element belongs to that practice — a Groundwork case study is orange because it is Groundwork, not because the grid needed variety. Never assign a practice color decoratively, and never introduce a fifth.

rules.name: The Fill / Ink Rule
rules.body: Every practice color exists twice: -fill for shapes you look at, -text for anything you read. Gooseberry and Trendy Orange fail AA on white outright. Setting text in a raw brand color on a light canvas is a contrast bug, not a style choice.

rules.name: The One CTA Rule
rules.body: There is exactly one call-to-action color site-wide (#00738b), and it is the darker ramp step rather than the raw brand blue, because the CTA has to carry white text at AA. A second CTA color anywhere on the site is a defect.

rules.name: The Ink-on-Color Rule
rules.body: All four fills clear 5.8:1 against near-black, which is why a saturated practice panel always takes ink type (#060709 at full, 84%, and 82% alpha for the three tiers) and never flips to white. Those alphas are set by the worst case — Vision red — where anything lower drops below AA.

rules.name: The Single Weight Rule
rules.body: Every heading in the system is weight 400. Tiers are set by size, and tracking tightens as size grows. Bolding a heading to make it more important breaks the system — add a size step or tighten the tracking instead. Only two weights ship: 400 for everything read, 600 for small UI that must be picked out. 500 and 700 were retired deliberately.

rules.name: The Mono Margin Rule
rules.body: The monospace voice annotates; it never leads. It is allowed on counters, section markers, tags, and metadata, and it sits in its own column. Never a headline, never body copy, and never stacked directly above a title where it becomes an eyebrow.

rules.name: The 14px Floor Rule
rules.body: No text on this site is smaller than 14px, including mono labels and legal copy. The floor was raised on purpose and it is why xs and sm sit unusually close together; they stay separate steps because xs is the label size and sm is small copy.

rules.name: The Shared Boundary Rule
rules.body: Where two same-canvas sections meet, both full paddings would stack into a gap twice the intended size, so each halves its padding at the shared edge. Sections that change canvas are excluded. This is automatic; do not hand-tune section padding to compensate for it.

rules.name: The Tone Rule
rules.body: Components reference the contextual --tone-* roles, never absolute colors. That is what makes re-tinting a whole section from light to dark a one-line class change instead of an edit to every color declaration in its module.

rules.name: The No-Shadow Rule
rules.body: No box-shadow with a blur or offset, anywhere, for any reason. If a surface needs to separate from what is behind it, change the canvas or add a hairline. A card that appears to float is off-system.

rules.name: The Surface / Control Split
rules.body: If you can read it, it is a surface and it is 4px. If you can click it, it is a control and it is 8px. If it is a token or a tag, it is a pill. There is no fourth case; a new radius value is almost always a mistake.

rules.name: The Matched Height Rule
rules.body: Every button is 3.5rem tall, stated on the base class rather than patched per variant, so a primary and a secondary side by side always align — arrow or no arrow.

rules.name: The Decorative-Only Rule
rules.body: Nothing in the texture layer may carry meaning, and nothing may sit above content or intercept a click. A bed is always z-index: -1 and always pointer-events: none.

rules.name: The Tooth Rule
rules.body: Grain is meant to be felt, not seen. It is held at 0.035 opacity and must never exceed roughly 0.06, above which it reads as noise sitting on the type rather than as tooth in the paper. It is fixed to the viewport, not scrolled with content, and it deliberately carries no blend mode.

rules.name: The Hairline Rule
rules.body: The divider vocabulary is exactly one item: 1px solid in #d8dade (or #b8bcc4 when it needs to hold its own). No dashed rules, no double rules, no 2px rules, no gradient dividers.

rules.name: The Practice Marker
rules.body: The one bar in the system that is not a divider: a 3px band across the top edge of a media frame, filled with the practice colour of the work inside it. A legend mark rather than a rule, which is why it is allowed a width the Hairline Rule forbids. Bounds are exact: 3px, top edge only, a practice -fill colour only, and only on a frame whose content belongs to that practice. An engagement spanning two practices splits the marker between them at a hard stop, never a blend; two is the limit. Any other edge, width, or colour is the side-tab anti-pattern.

dos: Do start a new section on paper. Light is home; the near-black canvas is punctuation that has to earn its place, and it gets full section padding on both sides when it appears.
Do set every heading at weight 400 and build the tier from size plus tracking.
Do reach for --tone-* inside components so the section stays re-tintable with one class.
Do put a texture on every surface. A flat, clean plane is off-system — pick the bed that fits (haze on light, one of the three dark grains on the inverse canvas, halftone on a transition).
Do use a practice color only where the content genuinely belongs to that practice, and take the -text step whenever the color carries type on white.
Do keep the monospace out in the margin, at 14px or above, uppercase, tracked at 0.12em.
Do separate planes with a single 1px hairline or a canvas change.
Do extend the reveal grammar to new surfaces, on the editorial easing for long settled reveals and the standard curve for state changes — always with a prefers-reduced-motion path.
donts: Don’t add a box-shadow with blur or offset. The tokens were removed on purpose; a floating card is off-system.
Don’t bold a heading to raise its importance, and don’t reach for weight 500 or 700 — both are retired and currently unreferenced anywhere in the codebase.
Don’t put a hex value in a component. Only tokens/palette.css holds hex; the guard is grep -rEn '#[0-9a-fA-F]{6}' src/components returning nothing.
Don’t set text in Gooseberry or Trendy Orange on a light canvas. Both fail AA outright.
Don’t introduce a second CTA color, or a fifth practice color.
Don’t stack a mono label directly above a title as an eyebrow. It belongs in the margin, in its own column.
Don’t drift toward the SaaS startup template: rounded-everything, purple-to-blue gradients, shadow-lifted cards on gray, or emoji feature icons.
Don’t drift toward agency showboating: gradient meshes, glow effects, autoplay hero reels, or any gesture whose subject is the firm's own taste.
Don’t drift toward corporate consultancy: navy-and-gray, stock handshake photography, or dense justified body copy where a story belongs.
Don’t drift toward brutalism: unstyled system fonts, harsh borders, or layout as provocation. This system's restraint is care, not a stunt.
Don’t add a new radius value. Surfaces are 4px, controls 8px, tags are pills; there is no fourth case.
